title: Using AI to do Market Research is not as helpful as you might think
author: RibBrit
selftext:
(written by me, not written by AI 😉 )

Using AI for trading information is not as helpful as you might think. 

When you ask AI to do market analysis, it will nearly always give you a favorable answer, twisting the truth to give you false hope. The answers are almost always a confirmation bias-loaded response. If you use AI, we recommend using it \\\*only\\\* as a tool amongst other tools, \\\*and\\\* we recommend asking whichever AI you are using to be critical. Example: Ask “why is this market a bad idea to trade on?” this will give you a clearer, more well-rounded idea of the risk involved. 

AI has a hallucination rate most certainly above 0% on any given AI tool. This means it is possible any or all of the information you are provided in your AI answer could be completely made up. This throttles even the best strategy. 

We highly recommend doing first hand information-gathering. Some of the tools we use personally are linked in my profile, in the linktree under Resources.

comments.author: Vegetable-Rub-8241
comments.body:
Ask it both ways on the same setup and you usually get two clean writeups that contradict each other. That is not analysis, that is framing.

We took the grade out of the model for that reason. Frozen rule set, then a separate scoring step on data it never saw. Wrong idea still dies. The number just cannot get talked upward afterwards.

Built that as Lagias, MCP for Claude Code / Cursor. Looking for a few design partners who actually iterate. DM if useful, "wrong for me" also fine.

comments.author: Fynca
comments.body:
This is pretty much what we heard too.

We spoke with close to 50 analysts while building our market research product, and almost nobody wanted AI to make the investment decision for them.

What they did want was AI that helps them research faster, find the relevant data, challenge their thesis and point out what they might be missing.

That’s a very different use case from asking ChatGPT if a stock is a good buy.

replies.author: RibBrit
replies.body: Absolutely. I havent dont market research on investor perception, but that is interesting to hear the analyst feedback. I have seen way too many posts on reddit and in my discord of people using AI as their only tool for investment decisions.

replies.author: RibBrit
replies.body: My BF and I, not an organization or anything just parents who trade for a living.

comments.author: Any_Object_4577
comments.body:
Yeah, this is pretty much where I landed too. Asking AI “is this a good trade?” is usually too open ended and you get a convincing answer either way.

I’ve found it much more useful when it’s grounded in actual historical data. Instead of asking for an opinion, I’ll ask something like “show me how this setup behaved across similar past markets” and use it more as a backtesting/research layer than a decision maker.

AI + real data feels way more useful than AI trying to create the thesis itself.

replies.author: RibBrit
replies.body: that is a better way to use AI as a tool… I think AI as a tool is great, just not as a full on position calculator.

comments.author: early_bird_7
comments.body: AI is useful in checking the formulas and finding any errors in programming. Adding new features to research strategy. However you need to have domain knowledge and point it to correct data otherwise it will find some junk on the internet and think it’s true.

comments.author: jdubspace
comments.body: Depends on your question and prompt. Claude gives me a bunch of not favorable answers. Nearly called me a degenerate gambler today when I felt I should hold longer on something.

replies.author: RibBrit
replies.body:
Claude has a \*more\* critical nature to it, particularly in what acts like a fail safe with toxic pattern recognition. That means if you ask it prompts \*about\* gambling it will give you answers, or it will protect itself by stating something along the lines of how it isnt able to provide guarantees and if you ask multiple similar questions about gambling odds, it will prompt a gambling source and ask about your personal safety net. The critical aspect of it is more to protect anthropic and hold to ethical standards. 

It still shouldn't be used as a primary or sole source for trading... in my opinion.
